answer_1.quote: In this work, we present a data generation approach to generate high-quality evidence conflicts, including answer and factoid conflicts.
answer_1.outputs: evidence pairs with answer and factoid conflicts

answer_2.quote: The results indicate the following: (1) LLMs frequently bias towards one of the conflicting evidence without stating reasons, accounting for 23.7% and 38.1% of the time for Claude 3 Sonnet and Haiku... (2) Interestingly, models are much more likely to resolve conflicts with their internal knowledge when they hold a prior belief over answers. (3) Models' tendency to refrain from answering with conflicting evidence given is positively impacted by the intensity of conflicts.

answer_3.quote: We consider an NLI check (such that q and e i entails a i ). ( ) an LLM reasoning check (such that an LLM can infer a i when given q and e i ). A piece of evidence is filtered out when it fails on any of the steps.

answer_4.quote: To investigate the data quality, we randomly sampled 200 pairs (50 each from {NQ-short, NQ-long, CWQ-short, CWQ-long}) for annotation. Given a question q, each pair or evidence (e i , e j ) is annotated by three independent annotators to determine its label from {Conflicting, Non-conflicting, Not sure}.
